name: Tulum Archaeological Site
shortDescription: Mayan ruins perched on cliffs overlooking the Caribbean, where ancient history meets turquoise waters.
description: Tulum stands as one of the few Mayan cities built on the coast, offering a unique perspective on how the Maya integrated their architecture with the natural landscape. The site's strategic location suggests it was an important trading port, and the view from the cliff-top temples remains one of the most photographed scenes in the Riviera Maya.

name: Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve
shortDescription: A UNESCO World Heritage site where mangroves, lagoons, and coral reefs create one of Mexico's most pristine ecosystems.
description: Sian Ka'an, meaning 'Origin of the Sky' in Mayan, protects over 1.3 million acres of tropical forests, mangroves, and marine habitats. This biosphere reserve is home to jaguars, manatees, and hundreds of bird species, offering a rare glimpse into the Yucatán's wild side.

name: Akumal Bay
shortDescription: A protected bay where sea turtles feed in shallow waters, creating a unique snorkeling experience just steps from shore.
description: Akumal, meaning 'Place of the Turtles' in Mayan, lives up to its name. The bay's seagrass beds attract green sea turtles year-round, making it one of the few places in the Riviera Maya where you can swim with these gentle creatures in their natural habitat.

name: Xel-Há Natural Park
shortDescription: A natural aquarium where a calm inlet meets the Caribbean, perfect for snorkeling among tropical fish without leaving the surface.
description: Xel-Há is a natural wonder where freshwater cenotes flow into a protected Caribbean inlet, creating a unique ecosystem. The calm, clear waters make it ideal for first-time snorkelers, while the surrounding jungle offers hiking trails and hidden cenotes to explore.

name: Cobá Archaeological Site
shortDescription: A sprawling Mayan city hidden in the jungle, where you can still climb the tallest pyramid in the Yucatán Peninsula.
description: Unlike the more polished sites, Cobá feels like a discovery. The ancient city spreads across the jungle, connected by sacbeob (white roads) that the Maya built. Climbing Nohoch Mul, the site's 42-meter pyramid, rewards you with views over the jungle canopy—a perspective the Maya themselves would have known.

name: Gran Cenote
shortDescription: A crystal-clear cenote where underground caves meet open water, creating a paradise for snorkelers and divers.
description: Gran Cenote is one of the most accessible and beautiful cenotes near Tulum. Its name means 'Great Cenote' and it lives up to it with extensive underwater cave systems and clear turquoise waters. The cenote connects to a network of underground rivers, making it a favorite among cave divers while remaining accessible to casual swimmers.

name: Cenote Dos Ojos
shortDescription: Two connected cenotes forming one of the world's most spectacular underwater cave systems, visible from the surface.
description: Dos Ojos, meaning 'Two Eyes', consists of two neighboring cenotes connected by a 400-meter underwater passage. The cenotes are part of one of the longest underwater cave systems in the world. The crystal-clear water and dramatic stalactite formations make it a world-renowned diving destination, while snorkelers can enjoy the surface beauty.

name: Cenote Calavera
shortDescription: A hidden cenote where you jump through a small opening into a deep, circular pool surrounded by jungle.
description: Cenote Calavera, also known as 'Temple of Doom', gets its name from the skull-like appearance of its three openings. The main entrance is a small hole in the ground, requiring a jump into the deep water below. The cenote's circular shape and surrounding jungle create an intimate, adventurous experience away from the crowds.

name: Puerto Morelos
shortDescription: A quiet fishing village where the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef meets a laid-back beach town atmosphere.
description: Puerto Morelos maintains its authentic fishing village charm despite being between Cancún and Playa del Carmen. The town's pier is a gathering place where locals and visitors watch the sunset, and the nearby reef offers some of the best snorkeling in the Riviera Maya. The relaxed pace and genuine hospitality make it a perfect escape from busier resort areas.

name: Cozumel Island
shortDescription: Mexico's largest Caribbean island, where world-class diving, Mayan history, and pristine beaches create a complete escape.
description: Cozumel is a world-renowned diving destination, home to the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System. Beyond the underwater wonders, the island offers Mayan ruins at San Gervasio, quiet beaches on the east coast, and a relaxed island atmosphere. The contrast between the developed west coast and the wild, undeveloped east coast showcases both sides of the Caribbean experience.

name: Isla Mujeres
shortDescription: A small island where golf carts replace cars, white sand beaches meet turquoise waters, and time moves at a different pace.
description: Isla Mujeres, just a 20-minute ferry ride from Cancún, feels like a different world. The island's narrow streets are perfect for exploring by golf cart, and the beaches on the north end offer calm, shallow waters ideal for families. The island's name, 'Island of Women', comes from Mayan times when it was dedicated to Ixchel, the goddess of fertility.

name: Cancún Beach
shortDescription: A 22-kilometer stretch of white sand where the Caribbean's turquoise waters meet a modern resort city.
description: Cancún's beach is the result of careful planning in the 1970s, transforming a small fishing village into Mexico's most famous resort destination. The beach's unique L-shape creates calm waters on one side and open ocean on the other, offering both protected swimming and dramatic wave-watching. The powdery white sand and clear blue water create the iconic Caribbean postcard scene.

name: Muyil Archaeological Site
shortDescription: An ancient Mayan port city hidden in the jungle, where a wooden walkway leads through mangroves to a lagoon.
description: Muyil, also known as Chunyaxché, was an important trading port connected to the Caribbean via a series of lagoons. The site is less visited than Tulum, offering a more intimate experience with Mayan architecture. A wooden boardwalk through the mangroves connects the ruins to Muyil Lagoon, where you can see how the Maya used waterways for transportation and trade.

name: Xcaret Park
shortDescription: A cultural and ecological park where Mayan traditions, underground rivers, and Caribbean wildlife create an immersive experience.
description: Xcaret combines natural beauty with cultural preservation, featuring underground river swims, Mayan archaeological sites, and live performances showcasing Mexican traditions. The park protects native flora and fauna while offering visitors a comprehensive introduction to the region's natural and cultural heritage. It's a place where entertainment and education merge seamlessly.

name: Punta Allen
shortDescription: A remote fishing village at the end of a jungle road, where the Caribbean meets the Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve.
description: Punta Allen is accessible only by a rough 50-kilometer road through the jungle, making it one of the most isolated communities in the Riviera Maya. The village's economy revolves around fly-fishing and ecotourism, with guides who know the waters intimately. The lack of development means pristine beaches, incredible stargazing, and a sense of being at the edge of the world.

name: Mahahual
shortDescription: A quiet beach town where the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef is just offshore, creating world-class snorkeling and diving.
description: Mahahual was a small fishing village until cruise ships began arriving, but it has maintained much of its laid-back charm. The town's long pier is perfect for watching sunsets, and the nearby reef offers some of the best snorkeling in the Caribbean. The relaxed atmosphere and proximity to pristine coral make it a favorite among divers and those seeking a quieter alternative to Cancún.

name: Bacalar Lagoon
shortDescription: The Lagoon of Seven Colors, where different depths create shades of blue that rival any Caribbean destination.
description: Bacalar Lagoon, also known as the Lagoon of Seven Colors, is a 42-kilometer-long freshwater lagoon fed by underground cenotes. The varying depths create stunning shades of blue, from turquoise to deep navy. The lagoon is home to stromatolites, some of the oldest living organisms on Earth, and offers a peaceful alternative to the ocean beaches of the Riviera Maya.

name: Cenote Cristalino
shortDescription: An open cenote with crystal-clear water perfect for swimming, surrounded by lush jungle vegetation.
description: Cenote Cristalino lives up to its name with exceptionally clear water that allows you to see every detail of the underwater world. The open-air cenote is ideal for families and first-time cenote visitors, with easy access and shallow areas. The surrounding jungle provides shade and a sense of seclusion, making it feel like a natural swimming pool hidden in the forest.

name: Cenote Azul
shortDescription: A large open cenote where deep blue waters invite swimming and cliff jumping in a natural setting.
description: Cenote Azul is one of the largest open cenotes in the area, with deep blue water that gets its color from the depth and mineral content. The cenote has both shallow areas for wading and deep sections for diving. Small fish swim alongside visitors, and the surrounding rock formations create natural platforms for jumping into the refreshing water below.

name: Playa Paraíso
shortDescription: A wide stretch of white sand where palm trees meet turquoise waters, creating Tulum's most photographed beach.
description: Playa Paraíso, or Paradise Beach, is Tulum's most iconic beach, with powdery white sand and clear turquoise water. The beach is wide and long, offering plenty of space even during peak season. Palm trees line the shore, providing natural shade, and the gentle waves make it perfect for swimming. The beach's name is no exaggeration—it truly feels like paradise.

name: Tulum Beach Zone
shortDescription: A bohemian beach strip where eco-lodges, yoga studios, and beach clubs create Tulum's unique coastal culture.
description: Tulum's beach zone stretches along the coast, where thatched-roof hotels and restaurants blend with the jungle. The area has become known for its bohemian, eco-conscious atmosphere, with yoga retreats, art galleries, and beach clubs that close early to preserve the natural environment. The combination of luxury and sustainability creates a unique destination that draws travelers seeking both relaxation and authenticity.

name: Cenote Carwash
shortDescription: A cenote once used to wash taxis, now a popular diving spot with clear water and underwater gardens.
description: Cenote Carwash gets its unusual name from its past use as a car wash for local taxis. Today, it's a popular cenote for both snorkeling and diving, with clear water and interesting underwater formations. The cenote has both open and cave sections, and the surrounding vegetation creates a natural, peaceful setting. It's less crowded than some of the more famous cenotes, offering a more intimate experience.

name: Soliman Bay
shortDescription: A secluded bay where calm waters and white sand create a peaceful alternative to busier beaches.
description: Soliman Bay is a hidden gem between Tulum and Akumal, offering a quiet beach experience away from the crowds. The bay's protected waters make it ideal for swimming and snorkeling, and the lack of development means you can enjoy the natural beauty without distractions. The bay is popular with locals and those in the know, offering a glimpse of what the Riviera Maya was like before mass tourism.

name: Cenote Jardín del Edén
shortDescription: A garden-like cenote where lily pads and tropical plants surround a clear, open pool perfect for swimming.
description: Cenote Jardín del Edén, or Garden of Eden Cenote, is an open cenote surrounded by lush vegetation that creates a garden-like atmosphere. The cenote is popular with both swimmers and divers, with clear water and interesting rock formations. The surrounding jungle provides natural shade, and the peaceful setting makes it feel like a hidden paradise, living up to its name.

name: Punta Maroma
shortDescription: A pristine beach where luxury resorts meet untouched nature, creating one of Mexico's most beautiful coastlines.
description: Punta Maroma is known for having some of the widest and whitest beaches in the Riviera Maya. The area is home to several luxury resorts, but the beach itself remains public and accessible. The combination of powdery sand, clear turquoise water, and lush vegetation creates a postcard-perfect setting. The beach's name comes from the maroma trees that once lined the shore.

name: Cenote Nicte-Ha
shortDescription: A small, intimate cenote where water lilies float on the surface, creating a serene and photogenic setting.
description: Cenote Nicte-Ha, meaning 'Water Lily' in Mayan, is a small but beautiful cenote known for its floating water lilies. The cenote is less visited than its famous neighbor Dos Ojos, offering a more peaceful experience. The clear water and natural light filtering through the opening create stunning visual effects, making it a favorite among photographers and those seeking a quieter cenote experience.

name: Playa del Carmen Beach
shortDescription: A vibrant beach where the pedestrian-friendly town meets the Caribbean, creating the Riviera Maya's social heart.
description: Playa del Carmen's beach runs parallel to Quinta Avenida, the town's main pedestrian street, creating a unique urban-beach experience. The beach is wide and sandy, with beach clubs and restaurants offering chairs and umbrellas. The combination of easy access, good restaurants, and beautiful water makes it a favorite gathering place for both locals and visitors.

name: Cenote Taak Bi Ha
shortDescription: An underground cenote accessible through a small opening, revealing a hidden world of stalactites and clear water.
description: Cenote Taak Bi Ha is a cave cenote that requires descending through a small opening to reach the water below. Once inside, the cenote reveals a stunning underground chamber with stalactites hanging from the ceiling and crystal-clear water. The cenote is popular with divers exploring the extensive cave system, but snorkelers can also enjoy the unique underground atmosphere.

name: Xpu-Ha Beach
shortDescription: A wide, calm beach where shallow waters and soft sand create an ideal setting for families and relaxation.
description: Xpu-Ha Beach is one of the most family-friendly beaches in the Riviera Maya, with shallow, calm waters and soft sand. The beach is wide and long, offering plenty of space even during busy times. A few beach clubs provide amenities, but much of the beach remains natural and undeveloped. The combination of easy access, calm water, and natural beauty makes it a favorite among those seeking a peaceful beach day.

name: Cenote Chac Mool
shortDescription: A cave cenote where dramatic light beams illuminate underwater formations, creating a photographer's dream.
description: Cenote Chac Mool is part of the same cave system as Dos Ojos and is known for its dramatic light effects. Sunlight filtering through openings in the cave ceiling creates stunning beams of light that illuminate the water and underwater formations. The cenote is popular with both divers and photographers, offering some of the most photogenic conditions in the Riviera Maya's cenote network.

name: Paamul Beach
shortDescription: A protected cove where calm waters and a small beach community create a peaceful escape from the main tourist areas.
description: Paamul is a small beach community with a protected cove that offers calm, shallow waters perfect for swimming and snorkeling. The area has a few small hotels and a beach club, but maintains a quiet, relaxed atmosphere. The cove's protection from open ocean waves makes it ideal for families, and the nearby reef offers good snorkeling opportunities.

name: Cenote Casa Tortuga
shortDescription: A complex of four different cenotes offering diverse experiences from open pools to cave diving.
description: Cenote Casa Tortuga is actually a collection of four cenotes on the same property, each offering a different experience. Visitors can explore open cenotes perfect for swimming, semi-open cenotes with partial cave coverage, and fully enclosed cave cenotes for diving. The variety makes it an excellent choice for groups with different interests and experience levels.

name: Punta Bete
shortDescription: A quiet beach area where small hotels and beach clubs offer a more intimate alternative to larger resort areas.
description: Punta Bete is a stretch of beach between Playa del Carmen and Puerto Morelos, offering a quieter alternative to the busier areas. The beach has several small hotels and beach clubs, but maintains a relaxed, low-key atmosphere. The combination of easy access, good restaurants, and beautiful beach makes it a favorite among those seeking a balance between convenience and tranquility.

name: Cenote El Pit
shortDescription: A deep cenote where sunlight creates a dramatic beam of light through the water, visible from 30 meters below.
description: Cenote El Pit is one of the deepest cenotes in the area, with a depth of over 40 meters. The cenote gets its name from its pit-like appearance, and the dramatic light beam that filters through the opening creates one of the most spectacular sights in the Riviera Maya's cenote network. The cenote is primarily for experienced divers due to its depth, but the visual spectacle makes it worth the journey.

name: South Akumal
shortDescription: A quieter section of Akumal's coast where fewer visitors mean more space and a more peaceful beach experience.
description: South Akumal offers the same beautiful beach and turtle-watching opportunities as the main bay, but with fewer crowds. The area has a few small hotels and condos, but maintains a residential, low-key atmosphere. The beach is just as beautiful, the water just as clear, and the turtles just as present, but with more space to enjoy it all.

name: Cenote Kantun Chi
shortDescription: An eco-park featuring four cenotes connected by jungle paths, offering a complete cenote experience in one location.
description: Cenote Kantun Chi is an eco-park that protects four different cenotes, each with its own character. Visitors can explore open cenotes, semi-open cenotes, and cave cenotes, all connected by well-maintained jungle paths. The park also includes a small Mayan temple replica and offers guided tours explaining the geological and cultural significance of cenotes.

name: Tankah Beach
shortDescription: A private-feeling beach where a few small properties share access to a beautiful, relatively undeveloped stretch of sand.
description: Tankah Beach is a quieter alternative to the main Tulum beach zone, with a few small hotels and private homes sharing access to a beautiful stretch of beach. The area feels more residential and less commercial, offering a glimpse of what Tulum was like before the tourism boom. The beach is just as beautiful, with the same white sand and turquoise water, but with a more intimate, local atmosphere.

name: Cenote Yax Kin
shortDescription: A small, intimate cenote where clear water and natural surroundings create a peaceful swimming experience.
description: Cenote Yax Kin is a smaller, less-visited cenote that offers a more intimate experience than the famous cenotes. The cenote has both open and covered sections, with clear water and natural rock formations. The smaller size and fewer visitors make it feel more like a local secret, offering a peaceful alternative to the more popular cenotes in the area.

name: Puerto Aventuras
shortDescription: A gated marina community where luxury condos, a dolphin center, and a protected beach create a resort-like atmosphere.
description: Puerto Aventuras is a planned community built around a marina, offering a different experience from the more organic beach towns. The community has luxury condos, hotels, restaurants, and a dolphin center, all within a gated area. The marina provides easy access to diving and fishing, while the protected beach offers calm waters perfect for families.

name: Cenote Sac Actun
shortDescription: Part of the world's longest underwater cave system, where divers explore a submerged world of stalactites and ancient formations.
description: Cenote Sac Actun is the entrance to the Sac Actun cave system, which at over 350 kilometers is the longest underwater cave system in the world. The system connects multiple cenotes and contains archaeological finds including human remains and artifacts from the Ice Age. While primarily for experienced cave divers, the cenote itself offers a glimpse into this incredible underground world.

name: Xcacel Beach
shortDescription: A protected turtle nesting beach where development is restricted, preserving one of the Riviera Maya's most pristine stretches of sand.
description: Xcacel Beach is a protected area due to its importance as a sea turtle nesting site. The beach has strict regulations limiting development and visitor numbers, which has preserved its natural beauty. The combination of pristine beach, clear water, and the knowledge that you're in a protected area creates a special sense of being in a place that's being carefully preserved for future generations.

name: Cenote Calavera Temple
shortDescription: An alternative entrance to Cenote Calavera, offering a different perspective on this unique cenote experience.
description: Cenote Calavera Temple refers to the temple-like structure that surrounds one of the openings to Cenote Calavera. The structure adds to the cenote's unique character, creating an almost ceremonial feeling when entering the water. The combination of the natural cenote and the man-made structure creates an interesting blend of natural and cultural elements.

name: Punta Soliman
shortDescription: A small point where Soliman Bay meets the open ocean, offering both protected and exposed beach experiences.
description: Punta Soliman is the point that separates Soliman Bay from the open ocean, creating two distinct beach experiences. On one side, the protected bay offers calm waters perfect for swimming and snorkeling. On the other, the open ocean provides waves and a more dramatic coastline. The point itself offers views of both, making it a great spot for understanding the geography of the Riviera Maya coast.

name: Cenote Manatí
shortDescription: A cenote named for the manatees that once frequented the area, now a peaceful swimming spot surrounded by jungle.
description: Cenote Manatí, named for the manatees that were once common in the area, is a beautiful open cenote surrounded by jungle. While manatees are rarely seen here today, the cenote maintains its natural beauty and peaceful atmosphere. The clear water and natural setting make it a great spot for a quiet swim away from the more popular cenotes.

name: Puerto Morelos Reef
shortDescription: Part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, where shallow waters and vibrant coral create world-class snorkeling just offshore.
description: Puerto Morelos Reef is part of the second-largest barrier reef system in the world, offering some of the best snorkeling in the Riviera Maya. The reef is close to shore, making it accessible for all skill levels, and the protected waters ensure calm conditions. The diversity of marine life and coral formations makes every snorkel trip a discovery.

name: Puerto Morelos Pier
shortDescription: A long wooden pier where locals and visitors gather to watch sunsets and fishing boats return with the day's catch.
description: Puerto Morelos Pier is the heart of the town, extending into the Caribbean and offering views of the reef and open ocean. The pier is a gathering place where the community comes together at sunset, and fishing boats dock with fresh catch. It's a perfect spot to understand the town's connection to the sea and its fishing heritage.

name: Puerto Morelos Beach
shortDescription: A wide, calm beach where the reef protects the shore, creating gentle waves perfect for families and relaxation.
description: Puerto Morelos Beach benefits from the nearby reef, which breaks the waves and creates calm, shallow waters. The beach is wide and sandy, with plenty of space even during peak season. The combination of calm water, good snorkeling access, and authentic town atmosphere makes it a favorite among those seeking a quieter beach experience.

name: Half Moon Bay
shortDescription: A crescent-shaped bay where calm waters and seagrass beds create ideal conditions for turtle watching and snorkeling.
description: Half Moon Bay lives up to its name with a perfect crescent shape that creates protected, calm waters. The bay's seagrass beds attract sea turtles, making it another excellent spot for turtle encounters. The bay is less crowded than the main Akumal Bay, offering a more intimate experience with these gentle creatures.

name: Cenote Yal-Ku
shortDescription: A lagoon-like cenote where fresh and salt water mix, creating a unique ecosystem perfect for snorkeling with tropical fish.
description: Cenote Yal-Ku is actually a lagoon where freshwater from underground cenotes meets saltwater from the Caribbean. This unique mix creates an environment where both freshwater and saltwater fish coexist, making it a fascinating snorkeling experience. The calm, clear water and abundance of fish make it ideal for families and first-time snorkelers.

name: Laguna Yal-Ku
shortDescription: A protected lagoon where the mixing of fresh and salt water creates crystal-clear conditions for snorkeling among colorful fish.
description: Laguna Yal-Ku is a protected natural aquarium where the unique combination of fresh and salt water creates exceptional clarity. The lagoon is home to hundreds of tropical fish species, and the calm conditions make it perfect for snorkeling. The area is well-maintained and protected, ensuring the ecosystem remains healthy for future generations.

name: Cenote Xcacel
shortDescription: A hidden cenote near Xcacel Beach, where clear water and natural surroundings create a peaceful escape from the coast.
description: Cenote Xcacel is located near the protected Xcacel Beach, offering a freshwater alternative to the ocean. The cenote is less developed than many others, maintaining its natural character. The clear water and surrounding jungle create a peaceful atmosphere, perfect for a refreshing swim after exploring the nearby beach.

name: Xcacel Turtle Camp
shortDescription: A sea turtle conservation camp where volunteers protect nesting sites and help hatchlings reach the ocean safely.
description: Xcacel Turtle Camp is a conservation project that protects one of the most important sea turtle nesting beaches in the Riviera Maya. During nesting season, volunteers monitor the beach, protect nests, and help hatchlings reach the ocean. The camp offers visitors a chance to learn about sea turtle conservation and witness this incredible natural process.

name: Río Secreto
shortDescription: An underground river system where you walk and swim through crystal-clear water surrounded by dramatic stalactite formations.
description: Río Secreto is an extensive underground river system that offers a unique experience of walking and swimming through crystal-clear water. The cave system features dramatic stalactite and stalagmite formations, some of which are still growing. The guided tours explain the geological history and Mayan significance of these underground rivers, making it both an adventure and an educational experience.

name: Casa Cenote
shortDescription: A unique cenote where fresh water flows directly into the ocean, creating a natural channel perfect for snorkeling and kayaking.
description: Casa Cenote, also known as Cenote Manatí, is unique because it connects directly to the ocean through a natural channel. The mix of fresh and salt water creates a unique ecosystem, and the channel is perfect for snorkeling, kayaking, or paddleboarding. The cenote's proximity to the ocean and its unique characteristics make it a favorite among water sports enthusiasts.

name: Cenote Maya Park
shortDescription: An eco-park featuring multiple cenotes, zip lines, and cultural activities, offering a complete cenote experience.
description: Cenote Maya Park combines natural beauty with adventure activities, featuring several cenotes, zip lines, and cultural demonstrations. The park offers a comprehensive experience of cenotes, from swimming in open pools to exploring cave systems. The addition of adventure activities and Mayan cultural elements makes it a popular choice for families and groups.

name: San Gervasio Archaeological Site
shortDescription: Cozumel's most important Mayan site, dedicated to Ixchel, the goddess of fertility, medicine, and the moon.
description: San Gervasio was the most important Mayan site on Cozumel, serving as a pilgrimage destination for women seeking fertility blessings from Ixchel. The site features several structures connected by sacbeob (white roads), and the peaceful jungle setting creates an intimate experience. Unlike the grand sites on the mainland, San Gervasio feels more personal and spiritual.

name: Cozumel East Coast Beaches
shortDescription: Wild, undeveloped beaches where the Caribbean meets dramatic cliffs, creating Cozumel's most spectacular coastline.
description: Cozumel's east coast is completely undeveloped, offering a stark contrast to the resort-lined west coast. The beaches here are wild and dramatic, with powerful waves crashing against rocky shores. The lack of development means you can experience the Caribbean as it was before tourism, with nothing but ocean, sky, and the sound of waves.

name: Punta Sur Eco Beach Park
shortDescription: Cozumel's southernmost point, where a lighthouse, lagoon, and pristine beach create a complete natural experience.
description: Punta Sur is Cozumel's southernmost point, home to a lighthouse, a crocodile-filled lagoon, and beautiful beaches. The eco-park protects this unique ecosystem while offering visitors access to beaches, snorkeling, and the lighthouse with panoramic views. The combination of natural beauty, wildlife, and history makes it one of Cozumel's most complete destinations.

name: Palancar Reef
shortDescription: One of the world's most famous dive sites, where massive coral formations create an underwater wonderland.
description: Palancar Reef is part of Cozumel's world-renowned diving scene, featuring massive coral formations that create canyons, swim-throughs, and walls. The reef is home to an incredible diversity of marine life, from colorful tropical fish to larger pelagic species. Whether diving or snorkeling, Palancar offers an unforgettable underwater experience.

name: San Miguel de Cozumel
shortDescription: Cozumel's main town, where colorful buildings, waterfront restaurants, and a relaxed island atmosphere create the perfect base.
description: San Miguel is Cozumel's only town, offering a perfect blend of island charm and modern amenities. The waterfront malecón is lined with restaurants and bars, while the colorful buildings and friendly atmosphere create a welcoming environment. The town serves as the perfect base for exploring the island, with easy access to beaches, diving, and Mayan sites.

name: Holbox Beach
shortDescription: A long stretch of white sand where shallow, warm waters and bioluminescence create a magical island experience.
description: Holbox Beach stretches along the island's north coast, offering miles of white sand and shallow, warm water. The beach is perfect for walking, swimming, and simply relaxing. At night, bioluminescent plankton can sometimes be seen in the water, creating a magical experience. The lack of cars and development makes Holbox feel like stepping back in time.

name: Punta Coco
shortDescription: Holbox's westernmost point, where shallow sandbars extend far into the water, creating a unique wading experience.
description: Punta Coco is Holbox's westernmost point, where sandbars extend far into the shallow water, creating a unique landscape. Visitors can walk far into the water, with the sandbars creating natural pools and channels. The area is popular for watching sunsets and is one of the most photographed spots on the island.

name: Whale Shark Tours
shortDescription: The world's largest aggregation of whale sharks, where you can swim alongside these gentle giants in their natural habitat.
description: Holbox is one of the best places in the world to swim with whale sharks, the largest fish in the ocean. From June to September, hundreds of whale sharks gather in the waters near Holbox to feed on plankton. The tours are strictly regulated to protect the animals, offering a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to experience these magnificent creatures up close.

name: Isla Pasión
shortDescription: A small, uninhabited island accessible by boat, where pristine beaches and clear water create a perfect day trip destination.
description: Isla Pasión is a small, uninhabited island just off Holbox's coast, accessible by boat tours. The island offers pristine beaches, clear water, and complete seclusion. A day trip to Isla Pasión feels like having your own private island, with nothing but sand, water, and the sound of waves.

name: Holbox Main Street
shortDescription: A sandy street where golf carts replace cars, colorful murals cover buildings, and island life moves at its own pace.
description: Holbox's main street is actually made of sand, with no cars allowed on the island. Golf carts and bicycles are the main modes of transportation, creating a relaxed, slow-paced atmosphere. The street is lined with restaurants, shops, and hotels, all painted in bright colors and often decorated with murals. Walking down the main street feels like being in a different world.

name: Holbox Bioluminescence
shortDescription: A natural phenomenon where bioluminescent plankton light up the water at night, creating a magical swimming experience.
description: Holbox is one of the few places where you can experience bioluminescence, a natural phenomenon where plankton in the water produce light when disturbed. Swimming at night in bioluminescent water feels like swimming through stars, with every movement creating trails of light. The experience is weather-dependent and best during new moon nights, making it a special and rare treat.
